Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.jdbc

Interface JdbcConnectionProvider

All Known Implementing Classes:
DataSourceConnectionProvider
public interface JdbcConnectionProvider
Supplies the JDBC connections a JdbcDriver works on, and takes them back.

A provider decides where connections come from and what giving one back means: closing it, returning it to a pool, or leaving it with an outer owner. Integrations that manage their own transactions implement this interface; a Spring provider, for example, acquires through DataSourceUtils.getConnection, releases through DataSourceUtils.releaseConnection, and reports true from inExternalTransaction(Connection) while Spring's transaction is active, so Diwan Database nests inside it with savepoints instead of committing it.

Implementation Requirements:
Implementations must be safe to call from several threads at once, because one driver serves every thread that uses the connection built on it.

    • inExternalTransaction

      default boolean inExternalTransaction(Connection connection) throws SQLException
      Reports whether the connection is inside a transaction owned by someone other than Diwan Database.
      Parameters:
      connection - a connection obtained from acquire(), never null
      Returns:
      true if an outer owner will commit or roll back the transaction
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the state cannot be determined
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default returns false. The driver asks once, right after acquire(), and keeps the answer for the life of the session.
